account:
Today I have heard repeated, unusually vague reports of a 'bridge or port change' at the bakery. One townsfolk report named baker, freight, innkeeper and neighbour as present, but I have not witnessed such a discussion or seen a proposal. The neighbour says they visited the bakery this morning but personally heard no discussion about changing the crossing and know of no definite proposal. They report no urgent river problems. I cannot establish whether the rumours concern any actual change, much less its purpose. I asked the secretary to seek firsthand details from the baker and report at our sixteen-thirty office appointment.

My ten o'clock mill inspection also lacked responsible staff or delivery records. I saw seventy-six hay bales and 104 emeralds in the mill stall, which is not a full stock audit. I asked the secretary to find the responsible contact and arrange a confirmed inspection. No council letters had reached the secretary when we spoke earlier.

I attended fifteen o'clock tea at the dockside cottage. Now, after I explained my sixteen-thirty office appointment and said goodbye, the neighbour has asked me to stay longer and walk to town hall around eighteen. That would conflict with my existing appointment. It may simply be a friendly invitation for company; I have no evidence of another purpose. I intend to keep my office appointment rather than infer motives from the invitation.
